cards.subject: Agamaggan
lines: A colossal boar Wild God, one of the first and most powerful things alive, who killed demons by the thousand with stomps and quills he threw like spears.
He fought Mannoroth and went down buying time for Malfurion to reach the Well of Eternity. The whole Razorfen is his body.

cards.subject: Willix the Importer
lines: A Ratchet goblin sent in to collect blueleaf tuber. The quilboar caught him.
He is standing in a dungeon full of pig-men worrying about margin: "There's blueleaf tuber in this trench! It's like gold waiting to be mined."
On the way out he looks up and says: "Blasted old crone."

cards.subject: You are walking on the vines
cards.tag: There is no stonework in here
lines: Directions inside this instance are given as landmarks in vegetation: cross over a large vine, past the first wooden bridge.
The paths are the thorn growth itself, with planks the quilboar have laid across the gaps.

cards.subject: Agam'ar
lines: The wild boars in here are not called boars. They are Agam'ar, named for the god.
Raging and rotting ones roam the same paths, and a hunter can tame them.
Everything down to the pigs carries a dead god's name.

cards.subject: Blood of Agamaggan
cards.tag: That is the mob's actual name
lines: Elite oozes wander the Kraul under that name, and they cast Curse of Blood.
Whether they are literally made of the demigod's blood, the wiki will not commit to.

cards.subject: Heralath Fallowbrook
cards.tag: The night elf in the hut
lines: A druid sent to find out what corrupted this place. The quilboar caught him, whipped him, and left him in a hut inside the dungeon.
A dwarf was thrown in the same cell. Heralath told him what he had learned, then died — that dwarf's journal lies at the foot of the Great Lift.
His last request is his wife's pendant, carried back to Darnassus.

cards.subject: Both rares do the same trick
lines: Each is a quilboar shaman who summons a Stone Rumbler to fight beside him.
Earthcaller is a rank, not a name. Geomancy — reading stones and crystals — is the quilboar's highest form of shamanism.

cards.subject: The Blind Hunter
lines: A rare elite bat, and an albino — pale where every other bat down here is dark.
The guess is that it is blind and colourless because it never leaves the deepest part of the Kraul.
It is tamable, and famously hard to make appear at all. In here it has no other name.

cards.subject: Aggem Thorncurse
lines: Prophet is a real title. The quilboar name their greatest shaman prophets of Agamaggan.
Where every other shaman in the game calls spirit wolves, he calls a boar.

cards.subject: Agathelos the Raging
lines: An enormous armoured boar kept in a short tunnel behind a magical field the quilboar maintain.
The story told about him is that the Death's Head fed him the guano off the Kraul's bats to make him bigger and angrier.
The caves above are full of bats. The droppings fall.

cards.subject: What the numbers were
lines: Uncapped at launch, capped at ten in patch 1.3.0, cut to five in 1.10.0.
In here it is five, and the range is twenty-nine to thirty-eight.
The twenty-four to twenty-nine everybody remembers is a Burning Crusade retune that has not happened.

cards.subject: What Charlga told her people
lines: She sent quilboar out to kill Barrens travellers by telling them the blood was needed to bring Agamaggan back.
It was a manipulation. She was separately negotiating with agents of the Scourge and quietly binding her own tribe to the undead.

cards.subject: She is not the top of it
lines: Charlga is the figurehead of the Razorfen and the Death's Head. A lich controls both.
The Death's Head are the first real Scourge foothold on Kalimdor.
Kill the Crone here and you have removed a middle manager. The answer is one dungeon further.
